title: Great Shepherd of Thy People, Hear
description: Great Shepherd of Thy People, Hear in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 27 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Blessing sought”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great Shep-herd of thy peo-ple, hear; Thy pre-sence now dis-play; We kneel with-in thy house of prayer; O, give us hearts to pray.

lines: Great Shepherd of thy people, hear;
We kneel within thy house of prayer;
O, give us hearts to pray.
The clouds which veil thee from our sight,
Dispose our minds to hear aright
Help us, with holy fear and joy,
O, make us, creatures of thy power,

licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
